findings.summary: Removing assertValidHeaderValue means header values with CR/LF are silently sanitized instead of throwing, which hides the bug from callers, mangles values, and drops an existing tested security behavior that callers and tests may expect.

judge.reason: Describes the known problem that values are silently sanitized instead of rejected.

findings.summary: INVALID_HEADER_VALUE_CHARS_RE silently strips all characters above U+00FF (non-Latin-1 text, CJK, emoji) and control characters like \x7F, so requests go out with altered header values such as Unicode filenames, instead of throwing or encoding.

judge.reason: Same defect: the regex strips characters above U+00FF at set time, so Unicode values are lost.

votes.label: hit
votes.reason: Same defect: the regex strips characters above U+00FF at set time, so Unicode values are lost.

findings.summary: Loopback aliasing makes a no_proxy entry of localhost also bypass 127.0.0.1 and ::1 (and vice versa), widening the match beyond standard exact-hostname NO_PROXY semantics and sending traffic direct that a user intended to proxy.

judge.reason: Describes the known loopback aliasing change in shouldBypassProxy.
